heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Bahamas
heroData.subtitle: Compliant hiring in the tax-neutral Caribbean
heroData.description: Onboard and manage your remote talent in the Bahamas without a local entity. Our EOR partners navigate the Employment Act 2001, handling National Insurance (NIB) contributions, localized contracts, and payroll taxation (0% income tax), allowing you to focus on growth in Nassau or Freeport.
heroData.bestFor: Companies hiring remote Caribbean talent or financial services professionals

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Local Alignment
steps.description: Drafting employment contracts that comply with the Bahamas Employment Act 2001. This includes defining the 40-hour work week, overtime rates (1.5x), and public holiday pay (2x).

steps.title: NIB Registration
steps.description: Assigning or verifying the employee's National Insurance Number. The EOR provider registers the employee under their local Bahamian entity for statutory reporting.

steps.title: Document Verification
steps.description: Collection of government-issued ID (Passport), proof of Bahamian residence, and bank account details for BSD/USD salary disbursement.

steps.title: Work Permit Initiation (if applicable)
steps.description: For expatriate hires, the EOR acts as the local sponsor for the Department of Immigration. This process can take 3-6 months and requires a Labor Certificate.

steps.title: First Day Induction
steps.description: Standardized onboarding regarding remote work policies, equipment delivery (if handled by EOR), and setup on the global HRIS platform.

items.title: 0% Personal Income Tax
items.text: Employees in the Bahamas are not subject to personal income tax. This makes the 'net take-home' pay significantly higher than in many other jurisdictions, even with NIB deductions.

items.title: Strict Termination Rules
items.text: The Employment Act 2001 requires 2 weeks' notice for employees with 6 months to 2 years of service, and 1 month's notice for those with 2+ years. Failure to provide notice requires 'pay in lieu'.

items.title: Novruz Holidays & Bonuses
items.text: Unlike some regions, there is no mandatory 13th-month salary in the Bahamas, but 'Christmas Bonuses' are a deeply ingrained cultural expectation in the private sector.

items.title: Probationary Periods
items.text: While 6 months is standard, the law allows up to 12 months for probation. During this time, termination notice requirements are typically minimal (usually 1 week).

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: Having a high-level executive working via an EOR in the Bahamas for literal years can occasionally risk triggering a Permanent Establishment for the parent company, especially if they are signing contracts locally.

items.title: Work Permit Quotas
items.text: The Bahamian government prioritizes 'Bahamianization'. Companies are expected to maintain a healthy ratio of local to expatriate staff, typically 3:1 or higher depending on the industry.

items.title: Employee Data Backup
items.text: Ensure your EOR provider has a robust Disaster Recovery plan. Given the hurricane risk in the region, digital data redundancy is a critical business continuity factor.

faqs.question: Are there specific notice periods for retirement?
faqs.answer: The Employment Act doesn't specify different notice for retirement, but mutual agreements are nearly universal for senior roles to ensure a smooth handover.

faqs.question: What happens if an employee is injured at home?
faqs.answer: The NIB 'Industrial Benefits' covers workplace injuries, including those for designated 'Work from Home' setups, provided the accident occurred during core working hours.

faqs.question: Can I provide a car allowance?
faqs.answer: Yes. This is a common and non-taxable (at the individual level) benefit in the Bahamas, though it should be clearly documented in the employment contract.

faqs.question: Is there a mandatory retirement age?
faqs.answer: No statutory retirement age exists in the private sector, but most companies align with the NIB pensionable age of 65.

faqs.question: Can an EOR hire short-term contractors?
faqs.answer: Yes, many EORs offer 'Contractor Management' which handles the compliance and payment for project-based work without full employment status.

faqs.question: Can I pay my Bahamian employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Bahamian Dollar (BSD) is pegged 1:1 with the USD. Many EORs allow for salary disbursement in USD, which is preferred by expatriates and high-level professionals.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory leave entitlements?
faqs.answer: Employees are entitled to 2 weeks of paid vacation after 1 year of service, increasing to 3 weeks after 7 years. Sick leave is typically 1 week per year but can be extended under specific medical conditions.

faqs.question: Is severance pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for redundancy. For employees with 1+ year of service, they are entitled to 2 weeks' pay for each year of service (capped at 24 weeks for non-managerial staff).

faqs.question: Are remote work expenses taxable?
faqs.answer: Since there is no personal income tax, reimbursements or stipends for internet and equipment are not taxed at the individual level.

faqs.question: What insurance is required for remote workers?
faqs.answer: Beyond NIB (which covers some disability), most professional employees expect private medical insurance, as public healthcare can have long wait times for specialized care.

faqs.question: How is the 13th month bonus handled?
faqs.answer: It is not mandatory, but if provided, it is usually paid in December. Since there is no income tax, the employee receives the full gross amount minus the 3.9% NIB.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for a director?
faqs.answer: Directors of an IBC are governed by the Articles of Association, but if they are also employees, the Employment Act's one-month notice rule typically applies.

faqs.question: Can an EOR sponsor a visa for a US citizen?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the 'Labor Certificate' must first be obtained to prove no Bahamian could do the job. This is the hardest part of the sponsorship process.

items.title: Relationship-First Business
items.text: Bahamian business culture is highly relational. Even in a remote EOR setup, occasional face-to-face meetings or video calls are valued more than purely transactional emails.

items.title: Standard Working Hours
items.text: The standard work week is 40 hours. Any work beyond 8 hours a day or 40 hours a week must be compensated at the overtime rate of time-and-a-half.

items.title: Public Holiday Observance
items.text: The Bahamas has many public holidays (Junkanoo, Whit Monday, etc.). If an employee works on these days, they MUST be paid double their standard rate by law.

steps.title: Time & Attendance Capture
steps.description: Recording 40 hours per week plus some overtime. Overtime is strictly regulated for non-managerial staff (8+ hours/day).

steps.title: NIB Contribution Calculation
steps.description: Calculating the 3.9% employee and 5.9% employer portions based on the weekly insurable ceiling ($740 as of recent updates).

steps.title: Net Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Since there is no income tax, net salary is 'Gross minus NIB'. Payment is typically made via direct deposit at local banks like RBC or CIBC FirstCaribbean.

steps.title: NIB Filing (C10 Forms)
steps.description: Submission of monthly contribution reports (Form C10) to the National Insurance Board by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Annual Reporting & Audit
steps.description: Preparation of annual earnings summaries for employees and verification for the Business License renewal process.

items.title: The C10 Form Deadline
items.text: All payroll contributions must be remitted to NIB by the 15th day of the month following the payroll period. Late submissions trigger a 5% penalty per month.

items.title: Salary Payment Frequency
items.text: By law, salaries must be paid at intervals of no more than one month. However, a bi-weekly or semi-monthly cycle (15th and end of month) is standard practice.

items.title: USD/BSD Parity
items.text: Always maintain a local BSD account for NIB payments even if you pay employees in USD. NIB only accepts Bahamian Dollars for statutory contributions.

items.title: Gratuities & Commissions
items.text: In the tourism and financial sectors, commissions and tips must be factored into the 'insurable earnings' up to the ceiling for NIB purposes.

faqs.question: Are there any local taxes for Nassau vs Freeport?
faqs.answer: Freeport (Grand Bahama) has certain exemptions under the Hawksbill Creek Agreement, but NIB contributions apply nationwide without regional variation.

faqs.question: What is the minimum wage in the Bahamas?
faqs.answer: As of early 2023, the national minimum wage rose to $260 per week ($1,126 per month) for both public and private sectors.

faqs.question: How are sick days paid?
faqs.answer: Employers pay for sick leave up to the limit defined in the contract or the Employment Act (usually 1 week). For long-term sickness, NIB provides 'Sickness Benefit' to the employee.

faqs.question: Can I withhold salary for damages?
faqs.answer: No. Under the Employment Act, an employer cannot make deductions from wages except for statutory requirements or with the express written consent of the employee.

items.title: Monthly NIB Remittance
items.description: Remit 9.8% total contribution to the nearest NIB local office or via the online portal.

items.title: Business License Return
items.description: Report annual turnover (which includes verified payroll records) for the Department of Inland Revenue.

items.title: NIB Contribution Statements
items.description: Provide employees with their annual summary of NIB deductions for their records.

steps.title: Gross Input & Ceiling Check
steps.description: The system takes the gross monthly or weekly wage and checks it against the NIB ceiling ($740/week or ~$3,207/month).

steps.title: NIB Portioning
steps.description: It applies 3.9% to the employee and 5.9% to the employer for the portion of earnings up to the ceiling.

steps.title: Tax Identification
steps.description: It verifies that no personal income tax or corporate income tax deductions apply to the salary.

steps.title: Net & Burden Output
steps.description: Finally, it subtracts the employee NIB from the gross for the 'Take-Home' and adds the employer NIB for the 'Total Cost'.

items.title: Net-to-Gross Calculations
items.text: When negotiating 'net' salaries with Bahamian candidates, employers must calculate backward to include the employee's 3.9% NIB portion to arrive at the true gross salary for the contract.

items.title: Overtime Inclusion
items.text: Remember that NIB must be calculated on the total gross, which includes overtime and any recurring stipends, as long as it doesn't exceed the ceiling.

items.title: Currency Fluctuations
items.text: While the BSD/USD is pegged, international wires may incur bank fees. Always ensure the 'final take-home' accounts for these if paying from a non-Bahamian bank.

faqs.question: Is the $740 ceiling per week or month?
faqs.answer: The ceiling is $740 per week, which translates to roughly $3,207 per month. Earnings above this threshold are not taxed for NIB.

faqs.question: Do I need to calculate VAT on payroll?
faqs.answer: No. Salaries are not subject to VAT. However, service fees from an EOR provider or an external payroll agency will have 10% VAT applied.

faqs.question: How are executive bonuses calculated?
faqs.answer: Bonuses are added to the gross for the month they are paid. If the total exceeds $3,207, the NIB is only calculated on that first $3,207.

faqs.question: Is the calculator updated for 2025?
faqs.answer: Yes, our tools are calibrated to the most recent NIB contribution tables and Business License thresholds current for 2025.

faqs.question: Does this work for part-time employees?
faqs.answer: Yes. The rates remain the same (3.9% / 5.9%), applied to the actual amount earned, provided it is above the minimum wage threshold.

faqs.question: What about the 1% industrial accident fee?
faqs.answer: In the Bahamas, this is included within the standard 5.9% employer contribution and is not a separate line item like in some other Caribbean nations.

faqs.question: Are there deductions for the ‘Public Purse’?
faqs.answer: No. Aside from NIB, there are no mandatory payroll-based social levies or defense taxes current in the Bahamian labor code for 2025.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Bahamas
heroData.subtitle: Global business setup in the premier Caribbean hub
heroData.description: Establish your International Business Company (IBC) or Domestic LLC in the Bahamas. Benefit from a tax-neutral environment, no corporate income tax, and the mature legislative framework of the IBC Act 2000, perfect for holding companies and international offshore operations.
heroData.bestFor: Asset protection, investment holdings, and international trade entities

steps.title: Choice of Entity Type
steps.description: Select between an International Business Company (IBC) for offshore activities or a Domestic Limited Liability Company (LLC) for local operations.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Register a unique name with the Registrar General's Department. Names must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corp', or 'S.A.'.

steps.title: Registered Agent Appointment
steps.description: Every Bahamian IBC MUST have a local Registered Agent and a Registered Office in the Bahamas. This agent facilitates all government filings.

steps.title: Filing of M&A
steps.description: The Memorandum and Articles of Association are filed digitally. Shareholder and Director names are maintained by the Agent (privacy is a key benefit).

steps.title: Business License & Tax ID
steps.description: Apply for a Business License from the Department of Inland Revenue (DIR) and obtain a TIN (Tax Identification Number) for VAT purposes.

items.title: Economic Substance Act 2018
items.text: Entities involved in 'relevant activities' (Banking, Insurance, Shipping, Holding) must demonstrate actual substance in the Bahamas to remain compliant.

items.title: Zero Corporate Tax
items.text: The Bahamas does not impose corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax on dividends for IBCs, making it a premier financial hub.

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: There is no legal requirement for directors or shareholders of an IBC to be residents of the Bahamas, allowing for 100% foreign ownership.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account without visiting?
faqs.answer: It is increasingly difficult. While some international banks allow for remote PoA setup, most corporate accounts requires the managing director's physical presence for KYB.

faqs.question: What is the minimum share capital for an IBC?
faqs.answer: There is no legal minimum paid-up capital. Most IBCs are registered with a standard authorized capital of $50,000, as this hits the lowest registration fee bracket.

faqs.question: Is a company secretary required?
faqs.answer: While not strictly mandatory for an IBC, most companies appoint one to manage the board minutes and ensure the Registered Agent has updated records.

items.title: Notarized Passports
items.description: Required for all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) and Directors.

items.title: Proof of Address
items.description: Utility bills or bank statements less than 3 months old.

items.title: Professional Reference
items.description: Letter from a lawyer or accountant for each major shareholder.

items.title: Source of Wealth Declaration
items.description: Detailed explanation of the origin of the company's funding.

items.title: Freeport Tax Benefits
items.text: Businesses operating within the City of Freeport (under the Hawksbill Creek Agreement) enjoy additional exemptions from certain duties and real property taxes until 2035.

items.title: VAT Registration Threshold
items.text: Mandatory VAT registration occurs when annual turnover exceeds $100,000. Voluntary registration is available for smaller businesses.

heroData.title: Staffing in Bahamas
heroData.subtitle: Recruit top-tier talent in Nassau and beyond
heroData.description: Access the Bahamian talent pool with 24/7 recruitment support. From expert financial analysts in the private banking sector to hospitality management specialists for the world-class tourism industry, we find the right fit for your remote or on-site team.
heroData.bestFor: Financial services firms and luxury hospitality brands

steps.title: Job Specification & Salary Benchmarking
steps.description: Aligning roles with local expectations. Management roles in Nassau often demand higher salaries due to the cost of living.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Sourcing
steps.description: Advertising on BahamasLocal.com, LinkedIn (highly active), and the Department of Labour's Job Exchange portal.

steps.title: Screening & Background Checks
steps.description: Verification of degrees (often from University of The Bahamas or US-based colleges) and police records as per sector requirements.

steps.title: Interview & Assessment
steps.description: Direct interviews focusing on both technical aptitude and soft skills essential for the relational Bahamian business culture.

steps.title: Offer Negotiation & Onboarding
steps.description: Finalizing the BSD/USD salary split (if applicable) and ensuring the employment contract aligns with the Employment Act 2001.

items.title: University specialized Talent
items.text: The University of The Bahamas (UB) produces strong graduates in Accounting, Law, and Tourism Management. Recruitment often peaks around graduation in May.

items.title: The Labor Certificate Requirement
items.text: Before hiring a foreigner, an employer MUST prove to the Department of Labour that no Bahamian is available for the role, a process known as getting a 'Labor Certificate'.

items.title: Skills in Demand
items.text: There is a significant shortage of specialized IT professionals (Cloud Architecture, FinTech development) in the local market, often requiring international searches.

items.name: Department of Labour 'Skills Bank'
items.description: National database for Bahamian job seekers and employers.

items.name: LinkedIn Bahamas
items.description: Primary professional networking site for corporate and tech talent.

items.name: Caribbean Jobs
items.description: Regional portal often used for senior management and specialized roles.

faqs.question: How long does it take to get a work permit?
faqs.answer: A short-term permit can take 4-6 weeks, while long-term permits (up to 3 years) can take 3-6 months depending on the industry and role.

faqs.question: What is the average notice period for professionals?
faqs.answer: For management roles, it is standard to require 1 month's notice, while for entry-level staff, 1-2 weeks is more common.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors instead of full-time staff?
faqs.answer: Yes, but ensure the contract clearly defines them as independent contractors to avoid retroactive employment claims under the Employment Act.

faqs.question: Are there mandatory employee health benefits?
faqs.answer: While NIB provides basic coverage, private health insurance is standard for professional roles and is a key factor in talent attraction.

faqs.question: IsJunkanoo leave a thing?
faqs.answer: While not statutory, many companies offer flexibility or half-days during the major Junkanoo festival periods (Boxing Day and New Year's Day).

items.title: Transportation Allowances
items.text: With no public rail system, most employees rely on private cars. A 'Mileage Allowance' or provided gas card is a valued perk.

items.title: Health Insurance (The Gold Standard)
items.text: Private health insurance with global cover is the single most important non-salary benefit for Bahamian professionals.

heroData.subtitle: Digital HR solutions for the Bahamas

steps.title: System Audit & Selection
steps.description: Verify the platform supports 0% income tax settings and the specific NIB weekly/monthly contribution ceilings.

steps.title: Employee Data Migration
steps.description: Securing sensitive NI Numbers and contract details into the database under local data privacy standards.

steps.title: Policy Configuration
steps.description: Defining vacation rules (2 weeks standard) and sick leave accruals as per the Employment Act 2001.

steps.title: User Training
steps.description: Onboarding the local HR team and employees onto the 'Self-Service' portal for payslip access and leave booking.

steps.title: Go-Live & Support
steps.description: Running a parallel payroll month with the old system to ensure NIB decimals are perfectly accurate before final rollout.

items.title: Data Privacy Compliance
items.text: The Data Protection (Privacy of Personal Information) Act 2003 governs how employee data must be stored. Cloud servers should ideally be in secure, recognized jurisdictions.

items.title: Custom NIB Formulas
items.text: Most international HRIS systems require custom math formulas to handle the NIB 'Ceiling' correctly, as it doesn't follow standard percentage-only rules.

items.title: Digital Payslips
items.text: While paper is still common, the transition to digital payslips via HRIS is highly encouraged by the Department of Inland Revenue for audit trails.

faqs.question: Does the system need to be hosted in the Bahamas?
faqs.answer: No, but it must comply with the Data Protection Act regarding the security and access of Bahamian citizens' data.

faqs.question: Can I integrate my Bahamian HRIS with global payroll?
faqs.answer: Yes, many modern platforms allow API integrations with international payroll providers, ensuring a single source of truth for all global employees.

faqs.question: Is tech support available in the EST timezone?
faqs.answer: The Bahamas operates on EST (UTC-5), so choosing a provider with North American support hours is crucial for local HR teams.

items.title: NIB Auto-Calculation
items.description: Built-in logic for the 3.9% / 5.9% split with current ceilings.

items.title: Multicurrency Support
items.description: Ability to display contracts in USD while paying in BSD.

items.title: Leave Management
items.description: Tracking of mandatory vs non-mandatory leave categories.

steps.title: Chart of Accounts Customization
steps.description: Developing a ledger that tracks BSD and USD transactions separately for accurate multi-currency reporting.

steps.title: VAT System Integration
steps.description: Setting up the 10% VAT tracking for all relevant sales and inputs to ensure monthly or quarterly DIR filings.

steps.title: Record Keeping Procedures
steps.description: Implementing digital backup systems to maintain 7 years of financial records as required by the Companies Act.

steps.title: Monthly Reconciliation

steps.description: Liaising with a BICA-certified accountant to prepare the necessary reports for the Business License renewal.

items.title: IFRS Standards
items.text: The Bahamas follows International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). All professional financial statements must adhere to these global norms.

items.title: The BICA Requirement
items.text: Any financial review or audit required by the government MUST be signed by a member in good standing of the Bahamas Institute of Chartered Accountants (BICA).

items.title: VAT Record Retention
items.text: The Department of Inland Revenue are very strict about VAT records. Maintain all tax invoices in a searchable digital format for at least 7 years.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late accounting records?
faqs.answer: Failure to keep proper records as required by the Companies Act can result in fines and complicates the mandatory annual Business License renewal.

faqs.question: Do I need a local bank account for bookkeeping?
faqs.answer: While an IBC can operate with an offshore account, a local account is practically necessary for paying local vendors, NIB, and Business License fees.

faqs.question: Is Quickbooks used in the Bahamas?
faqs.answer: Yes, Quickbooks Online is the most popular accounting software for local SMEs and international IBCs due to its ease of multi-currency setup.

faqs.question: Can my accounting be done remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the digital platform allows for cloud access. However, ensure your accountant is familiar with the DIR's VAT filing portal requirements.

items.title: BICA Member Search
items.description: Verify your auditor is a licensed member of the Bahamas Institute of Chartered Accountants.

items.title: DIR VAT Portal
items.description: The online system for all indirect tax reporting and payments.

items.title: NIB Employer Portal
items.description: Used to cross-reference payroll accounting with statutory payments.

steps.title: Business License Renewal
steps.description: Submission of verified turnover figures and proof of NIB compliance. Deadline: March 31st.

steps.title: Economic Substance Declaration
steps.description: Filing via the portal to confirm if the entity performed 'relevant activities' during the fiscal year. Deadline: 9 months after year-end.

steps.title: FATCA/CRS Reporting
steps.description: For financial institutions, reporting of account holder information to the Competent Authority. Deadline: September 30th.

steps.title: AML/KYC Audit
steps.description: Annual internal review of client files and transaction monitoring policies to prevent financial crime.

items.name: DIR Online Portal
items.description: Primary gateway for VAT and Business License filings.

items.name: NIB Employer Self-Service (ESS)
items.description: Portal for tracking contribution history and employee registrations.

items.name: Economic Substance Portal
items.description: Dedicated site for annual substance declarations.

items.title: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)
items.text: For Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or high-risk sectors, Bahamian compliance officers will require proof of the original source of wealth stretching back decades.

items.title: Record Keeping Compliance
items.text: All KYC documents must be updated every 2-3 years for active clients to ensure that all information remains current and accurate under Central Bank guidelines.

faqs.question: What happens if I fail the Economic Substance test?
faqs.answer: Initial failure leads to a fine and a requirement to remediate. Persistent failure can lead to fines up to $300,000 and the company being struck off the register.

faqs.question: How do I prove local substance?
faqs.answer: Substance is proven by having a local physical office, local expenditures commensurate with activity, and local board meetings with qualified personnel present.

faqs.question: Is there a register of beneficial owners?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it is not public. The Register of Beneficial Ownership (RBO) is a secure, private database accessible only by Bahamian law enforcement and regulatory authorities.

faqs.question: Are PEPs prohibited from owning companies?
faqs.answer: No, but they are subject to much higher scrutiny and mandatory 'Enhanced Due Diligence' by both the Registered Agent and any local banks.

items.title: Central Bank of The Bahamas
items.text: Regulates the banking and trust sector, ensuring monetary stability and managing exchange controls.

items.title: Securities Commission
items.text: Oversees the investment funds, securities, and capital markets, including the new DARE Act for digital assets.

items.title: Insurance Commission
items.text: Responsible for the prudential supervision of all insurance companies operating in and from within the Bahamas.

items.title: The Business License Tax
items.text: Instead of corporate income tax, the Bahamas charges a tax based on gross turnover. This ranges from $100 (for very small businesses) up to 1.5% for specific sectors.

items.title: VAT Filing Frequency
items.text: Businesses with turnover over $5M file monthly; others typically file quarterly. The deadline is strict: the 21st day of the month following the period.

items.title: Property Tax Exemptions
items.text: First-time homeowners (Bahamians) and certain industrial projects in Freeport can apply for significant Real Property Tax exemptions.

faqs.question: Is there a withholding tax on dividends?
faqs.answer: No. The Bahamas does not impose any withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss my VAT filing?
faqs.answer: The penalties are severe, starting at $1,000 per missing return and increasing with the amount of tax owed. It is critical to file even if you have 'zero' activity.

faqs.question: What is the real property tax rate?
faqs.answer: For commercial property, it is typically $1,000 plus 1% on the value over $500,000. Rates are lower for residential properties.

steps.title: Threshold Monitoring
steps.description: Reviewing cumulative 12-month turnover to detect when it crosses the $100,000 mandatory threshold.

steps.title: DIR Registration Application
steps.description: Submitting company documents, bank details, and turnover projections via the DIR Online Portal.

steps.title: VAT Certificate Issuance
steps.description: Receiving the official TIN and VAT certificate, which must be clearly displayed at the place of business.

steps.title: System Alignment
steps.description: Updating invoices and accounting software to include the 10% VAT charge and show the mandatory TIN.

items.title: VAT Filings
items.description: 21st of each month (Monthly) or 21st of the month following the quarter end.

items.title: Business License
items.description: Renewal application by January 31st; Payment due by March 31st.

items.title: Real Property Tax
items.description: Due by March 31st each year to receive potential early-payment discounts.

steps.title: Data Protection Provisions

steps.title: Dispute Resolution (Arbitration)

steps.title: Payment Terms in USD

items.title: Employment Act 2001
items.description: The primary statute governing all labor relations in the Commonwealth.

items.title: International Business Companies Act
items.description: The law defining the structure and rights of offshore companies.

items.title: Data Protection Act 2003
items.description: Governing the handling of personal information.

faqs.question: Can I use US law for a Bahamian contract?
faqs.answer: You can for commercial B2B contracts, but for employment, Bahamian law (Employment Act 2001) is mandatory and overrides any foreign law choice.

faqs.question: How long does a civil lawsuit take in the Bahamas?
faqs.answer: The court system can be slow. It is highly recommended to include mediation or arbitration clauses to resolve disputes within months rather than years.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses enforceable?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must be 'reasonable' in terms of duration (usually 6-12 months) and geographic scope. Overly broad clauses are often struck down by courts.

faqs.question: Do I need a local lawyer to draft an MSA?
faqs.answer: While not strictly required for B2B, having a local legal review is vital to ensure that clauses regarding local taxes and data privacy are fully compliant.

items.title: Work-for-Hire Default
items.text: Under Bahamian law, IP created by an employee during the course of employment generally belongs to the employer, but explicit clauses in the MSA are highly recommended for clarity with contractors.

items.title: Data Protection Fines
items.text: Breaching the Data Protection Act can lead to fines up to $100,000. MSAs must include robust indemnity clauses specifically covering data privacy breaches.
